facts.fact: Every load converts every Gaussian, allocates canonical/projected/count/offset/scan buffers sized by the full asset, and memcpy()s the full canonical Gaussian array.
Scene loading creates a new GaussianPipeline and calls load() for the whole Gaussian asset; no patch/update API is present.
ResponsiveGaussianCount bounds live projection/sort/composite work while the full Gaussian asset remains resident; it does not add revision-level GPU patch updates.
The current frame path projects/scans/generates keys over gaussianCount_ before sorting/compositing. Revision-application locality and per-frame visibility/render locality are distinct problems.

oneMillionGaussianAccounting.note: ~344 MB before scan-block state and tile-key/value/range buffers. This is allocation footprint accounting, not measured resident GPU memory.

decision: PROMOTE REVISION-APPLICATION GPU LOCALITY AS A REQUIRED DEPENDENCY-CLOSURE LAYER. Do not conflate it with per-frame visibility/sort acceleration.
survivingMechanisms: same-cardinality in-place canonical record updates for changed slots/ranges
stable slot/free-list or chunked region storage for split/merge/prune without whole-buffer rebuild
explicit active/tombstone semantics if capacity exceeds live primitive count
later: dirty/visible regional dispatch if profiling shows per-frame global projection is dominant
killConditions: If stable-slot maintenance causes unacceptable fragmentation or scan cost that outweighs reload savings, abandon stable slots.
If Metal shared-buffer patching does not reduce measured revision latency/bytes on M2 Pro, do not claim renderer update locality.
If primitive reorder requirements force global record motion under the chosen renderer, use region/chunk indirection instead of pretending slots are stable.
